In the time before time, when the sky was an endless void of black, there lived a lonely weaver named Astra. She dwelt at the edge of the world, spinning thread from moonbeams and silence.

One night, Astra wept, for her tapestries, though beautiful, hung unseen in the darkness. Her tears fell upward, and where each droplet touched the void, it burst into brilliant flame.

"What have I done?" she gasped, watching the lights multiply across the emptiness.

A voice echoed from the new lights: "You have given the darkness meaning. But your work is not finished."

When her work was complete, Astra herself became light, taking her place among her creations. Now, on clear nights, we see her tapestry stretching across the heavens.

And the stars still whisper her truth: that even in the deepest darkness, connection and story can illuminate the void.
